agent_priors_used: General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): augmentation overhead is the default failure mode; memory/skill modules pay retrieval and maintenance cost on every task, so gains often vanish once comparators receive an equal inference budget - this forces a budget-matched vanilla/strong baseline and total-token accounting in any future C-LLM-INHERIT/C-PRODUCT-ECON run, and is consistent with the external 2026 finding that a token-matched vanilla actor can match online skill/memory modules.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): long-horizon agents fail mainly through early subplanning errors that propagate path-dependently and through loss of durable constraints; SPIDER value should be expressed as reduced residual novelty plus a re-surfaced verification/constraint layer, measured on trajectory-level diagnostics.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): stable procedures/mechanisms transfer far more reliably than ephemeral site values, so caching the 'how' while re-reading the 'what' is the defensible product thesis; this directs attention to freshness/invalidation economics rather than to universal Web dynamics.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): deterministic accessibility-first locators plus calibrated abstention are becoming commodity, so semantic resolution is likely a supporting capability and market-level moat claims need competitor-strength controls (e.g. native Stagehand-like caching), not four internal arms alone.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a research factory over-produces near-duplicate measurement-invalid packets when an upstream prerequisite (substrate availability, task-bank dynamic range, model endpoint) is unsatisfiable and unaddressed; repair or explicitly park the prerequisite once instead of re-running the ladder.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a single-vantage/single-window measurement is an external-validity trap, but if a second vantage cannot be provisioned the honest output is the exact substrate blocker, not another single-vantage run.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): idle parallel capacity has opportunity cost; an idle lane should be pointed at the highest-value unblocked question rather than left dormant or re-run on a completed thread.

General agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a low completion-token count (~10-15 tokens) with zero answer actions is consistent with an action/observation-space or stopping-signal failure rather than a pure reasoning-capacity ceiling, which is why the representation probe is the cheapest next B3 discriminator.

allocation.question: On the byte-verified credential-free local models (M-14B-QWEN, M-8B-LLAMA) and the frozen minimal multi-step Web-agent protocol, does the audited failure mode - step-0 reveal succeeds and PAGE_TEXT contains the target, yet the model emits a hidden-button re-click loop with zero answer actions - resolve when the observation/action representation is the single varied factor (suppress the hidden reveal button from the ELEMENTS observation; and/or present a full accessibility-tree observation) so that representation failure is separated from raw multi-step control capacity; i.e. do either local class reach answer_action_emission_rate > 0 and task_success_rate >= 0.6, or does the failure persist across observation changes - in which case B3 is credential-gated and the exact human-issued credential/endpoint blocker is recorded instead of another ladder re-run?
allocation.rationale: B3 is the single binding blocker on the program's one decisive unrun measurement, and the last Intel mandate's stop rule has fired: re-running the same local ladder under the same protocol is a spent thread, and 0 of 12 hosted providers are provisionable without a human credential, so the only autonomous path to B3 is to test whether the failure is observational rather than a capacity ceiling. Decision counterfactual: if the observation change makes a local class clear the frozen bar, B3 is satisfied and the flagship four-arm benchmark unblocks without any credential; if the failure persists across observation representations, B3 is established as credential-gated and the program stops spending cycles rediscovering the same absence and records the exact human-issued prerequisite - either branch changes the program's next step. Strongest fair baseline: the SAME frozen GBNF/temperature-0/seeds-42-46 protocol and byte-verified GGUFs with the current ELEMENTS observation, whose step-1 parseable-action rate is already 1.0 and positive controls 10/10, so a gain is attributable to the observation factor and not to decoding; the frozen bar (task_success_rate >= 0.6 AND parseable_action_rate_step1 >= 0.6) is unchanged. Validity and dependency: the probe reuses the parent's byte-verified served-body pins and frozen runner/fixture and needs no credential; the ELEMENTS observation change is the only varied factor and must be bound by sha256 at freeze; the low mean completion-token counts (~10-15) with zero answer actions in the parent are consistent with an action/stopping representation defect, which is exactly what this separates. Budget and stopping: one orthogonal observation-factor probe on the two already-tested classes, with the accessibility-tree arm included only if it is cheap; stop once, and if neither observation change alters the failure mode, record B3 as credential-gated rather than re-running ladders. Opportunity cost: another hosted-provider census or the same GGUF ladder would reproduce the spent thread; competitor-baseline/task-bank reproduction is deferred because without a capable agent no flagship comparison can run.
